Drift diffusion model for choice and response time

Source: R/ctModelDDM.R
ctModelDDM.Rd

Builds a ctsem model of choices and response times by the drift diffusion model, with the drift as a latent process. The model is an ordinary ctModel with one choice and response time indicator (manifesttype = 5), so it is fitted with ctFit and can be changed or extended like any other model, for example with other indicators of the same latent process.

Usage

ctModelDDM(
  name = "rt",
  drift = ~1,
  boundary = ~1,
  ndt = ~1,
  bias = 0.5,
  random = c("drift", "boundary", "ndt"),
  dynamic = FALSE,
  sv = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

name

Name of the data column holding each trial's response time in seconds, negative for a response at the lower boundary. With columns rt and correct, dat$rt_signed <- ifelse(dat$correct == 1, dat$rt, -dat$rt) makes it for accuracy coding.

drift, boundary, ndt

One sided formulas of trial level predictors of the drift, the log boundary separation and the log nondecision time, such as ~ speed + difficulty. ~ 1 for none. Predictors are numeric columns of the data, entered as time dependent predictors. A factor needs dummy columns. The drift's predictors shift the drift on their trial only.

bias

The relative start point, as a proportion of the boundary separation from the lower boundary. A number fixes it, and a one sided formula estimates it, with predictors on the logit scale.

random

Which of 'drift', 'boundary', 'ndt' and 'bias' vary over subjects.

dynamic

Whether the drift changes over the session. FALSE keeps each subject's drift constant. TRUE makes it a mean reverting (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck) process in the data's time column around the subject's level, starting from its stationary distribution. The time column sets the scale of its rate: trial number, or seconds.

sv

Whether to estimate trial to trial variability of the drift, as a standard deviation.

...

Passed to ctModel, such as id, time or TIpredNames.

Value

A ctStanModel object.

Details

The drift's parameters are named drift_mean (its mean, or with dynamic = TRUE drift_cint, drift_auto and drift_diffusion for the process's intercept, auto effect and diffusion), boundary, ndt and bias, and each predictor's effect <parameter>_<predictor>. The diffusion coefficient of the decision process is 1.

See also

ctModel, whose WIENER argument sets the boundary, nondecision time and bias of a choice and response time indicator directly.

Examples

m <- ctModelDDM(name = 'rt_signed', drift = ~ difficulty, boundary = ~ speed,
  dynamic = TRUE)
print(m)
